issues.description: The manuscript gives mutually incompatible descriptions of when the interventions occur. One section says warnings are after collaborative recall, another says the resistance methods are before collaborative recall, and the procedure places them after collaborative recall. This is critical because the theoretical rationale differs for inoculation before misinformation versus correction/warning after misinformation, and the study cannot be replicated or interpreted without a single specified timing.
issues.quote: "In the present study we decided to place the warning after the collaborative recall" ... "What is important, we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation before the collaborative recall phase" ... "The procedure will consist of four main phases: (1) presenting the original material, (2) collaborative recall (including misinformation), (3) three procedures to reduce vulnerability to misinformation (and a control condition), and (4) an individual memory test"

issues.description: The manuscript claims that discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced, but later states that every pair will discuss the same four critical details. If the same details are always discussed, discussion status is completely confounded with item identity, salience, baseline memorability, and difficulty. Any difference between discussed and non-discussed details may therefore reflect item differences rather than memory conformity.
issues.quote: "discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced" ... "In order to ensure sufficient discussion, each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase."

issues.description: The final memory test is described as open-ended in the procedure but as two-alternative forced choice in the analysis plan. These formats produce different response processes, guessing rates, scoring rules, and comparability with previous MORI studies. This inconsistency makes the planned outcome and analysis unclear and prevents replication.
issues.quote: "The test will contain 20 open-ended questions" ... "In the present research, the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format."

issues.description: The analysis plan gives two incompatible approaches to identifying misinformation exposure. It first says partner responses that match the participant's version or 'don't know' are not misleading, but then says all discussed items will be categorized as containing misinformation. This will misclassify trials in which no misleading information was actually provided, bias effect estimates, and obscure the mechanism of conformity.
issues.quote: "However, if the partner provided an answer consistent with what the participant had seen, that is, “white mug” (such a situation can happen, e.g., as a result of the partner's guessing), the situation will not be classified as misleading. Of course, the answer ‘don’t know’ will also not be classified as misleading." ... "we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation"

issues.description: Participants are tested in pairs, discuss with each other, and appear to be assigned to condition as pairs, but the proposed ANOVA treats 240 individuals as independent observations. Responses within dyads are necessarily correlated because partners influence each other and share the same discussion. Ignoring dyadic clustering inflates degrees of freedom, underestimates standard errors, and can produce false-positive intervention effects.
issues.quote: "The sample size will be set at 240 people (120 pairs)." ... "Pairs of participants will be randomly assigned to one of four groups" ... "The results will be analyzed by means of a two-factor ANOVA"

issues.description: The power calculations are based on individual participants, but the intervention is administered at the dyad/session level and outcomes are clustered within dyads. The effective sample size is closer to 120 dyads, not 240 independent participants, and may be lower depending on intraclass correlation. Therefore the reported power for intervention effects is likely overstated.
issues.quote: "The sample size will be set at 240 people (120 pairs)." ... "Considering the accessible financial, organizational and time resources, a sample of 240 participants was assumed"

issues.subcategory: inappropriate model for bounded repeated item data
issues.description: The primary outcomes are counts or binary item-level responses based on only a few critical items per participant. ANOVA on counts assumes approximately normal residuals and does not model item-level binomial variance, participant clustering, dyad clustering, or item heterogeneity. A generalized linear mixed model with random effects for participant, dyad, and item would be more appropriate.
issues.quote: "Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test: the number of: (1) correct answers (consistent with the movie), (2) answers consistent with the misinformation, (3) other answers (consistent neither with the movie nor the misinformation), and (4) the overall number of answers." ... "The results will be analyzed by means of a two-factor ANOVA"

issues.description: Only eight critical details are available, with four discussed and four non-discussed. This produces low measurement reliability and makes results highly sensitive to idiosyncratic item difficulty, especially given the lack of actual counterbalancing. It also limits the ability to generalize beyond the specific details selected.
issues.quote: "Both versions are identical except for eight critical details" ... "the participants will discuss half of the dissimilar details"

issues.description: The analysis plan lists multiple outcomes—correct answers, misinformation-consistent answers, other answers, total answers, and average accuracy on filler/non-discussed/discussed questions—without specifying a primary endpoint. This creates analytic flexibility and increases the risk of selective interpretation and inflated Type I error.
issues.quote: "We will explore the individual memory test’s scores for the critical details using analysis of variance (ANOVA), using all four indices: the number of correct answers, number of answers consistent with misinformation, other answers, and the overall number of answers. Moreover, we will observe the individual memory test’s average accuracy on the filler, non-discussed, and discussed questions."

issues.description: The manuscript proposes a general interaction, follow-up comparisons between groups, analyses of four outcome indices, and additional exploratory analyses, but does not specify multiplicity correction or a hierarchical testing strategy. This increases the probability of false-positive conclusions.
issues.quote: "In the case of a significant main interaction, follow-up comparisons between pairs of groups will be performed." ... "Comparisons among all groups and directional significance tests are assumed."

issues.description: The authors plan directional significance tests despite acknowledging that at least one intervention could plausibly increase memory conformity. One-tailed/directional tests are not appropriate when theoretically plausible effects exist in both directions.
issues.quote: "If this is the case, increased memory conformity is possible." ... "Comparisons among all groups and directional significance tests are assumed."

issues.description: Efficacy is defined as a smaller difference in accuracy between discussed and non-discussed items. This difference can shrink because an intervention improves discussed-item accuracy, worsens non-discussed-item accuracy, changes response criterion, increases omissions, or affects both item types. Thus the proposed criterion may label an intervention effective even if it harms overall memory performance.
issues.quote: "The efficacy of a given method will be confirmed if the magnitude of memory conformity (expressed as the difference between the accuracy on discussed and non-discussed items) is smaller in the group in which this method was applied than in the control group."

issues.description: The study is powered only for conventional medium and large effects because no expected effect size is available. The manuscript does not define a smallest effect size of interest or justify why smaller effects would be theoretically or practically unimportant. Null findings will therefore be difficult to interpret.
issues.quote: "no data exists that would allow the expected effect size to be estimated" ... "the power analysis was done in the standard way for a small, medium, and large effect, according to the existing conventions" ... "this allows for excellent power to detect medium and large effect sizes but not small ones"

issues.description: The replication power analysis combines only two prior effect sizes that differ dramatically. A random-effects estimate from two studies is highly unstable and the manuscript provides no heterogeneity estimate, confidence interval, or sensitivity analysis. The assumed effect size may be unreliable.
issues.quote: "The existing results as regards effect sizes are Hedges’ g = 1.92, N = 55 (Ito et al., 2019) and Hedges’ g = 0.38, N = 74 (Kękuś et al., 2020). Given the rather large difference in effect sizes between both studies, random effects were assumed while calculating the joint effect size, which was 1.13."

issues.description: The three interventions differ on many dimensions simultaneously: content, specificity, directness of warning, interaction, length, task demands, emotional content, motivation, and experimenter involvement. Therefore differences between interventions cannot identify which theoretical component caused any effect.
issues.quote: "These are (1) Extended warning against misinformation, (2) providing detailed knowledge about the fallibility of memory (we called this method Education about memory), and (3) demonstrating the vulnerability of memory and motivating subjects to overcome it (called Demonstration and motivation)."

issues.description: The authors acknowledge overlap among interventions but suggest empirical results may determine whether overlap is substantial. However, because the interventions are bundled and not factorially manipulated, the study cannot disentangle shared versus unique mechanisms even if outcome differences are observed.
issues.quote: "we are aware of some overlap between the three interventions, for instance, teaching about memory is included is present in a way in both Education about memory and Demonstration and motivation. Empirical results may help to determine to what extent the overlap is substantial"

issues.description: The extended warning appears to tell participants the deception and that the partner saw a different movie before the final memory test. This may transform the final test into an instruction-compliance or source-discounting task rather than a test of memory conformity. It also makes the condition fundamentally incomparable to conditions that do not receive equivalent disclosure.
issues.quote: "Extended warning, informing that the partner actually saw a different version of the movie and informing why the deception was applied"

issues.description: The Demonstration and motivation condition explicitly encourages participants not to rely on information from the partner. Any reduction in partner-consistent answers may reflect compliance with explicit instructions rather than reduced susceptibility, improved source monitoring, or memory protection.
issues.quote: "The participants will be strongly encouraged to rely only on their own memory, not on any information stemming from the partner."

issues.subcategory: control condition not inert or matched
issues.description: The control podcast concerns soft skills and social attitudes, which may itself affect interpersonal conformity, trust, or willingness to rely on a co-witness. It is also unclear whether it is matched to the intervention conditions for length, arousal, relevance, and cognitive engagement.
issues.quote: "In the control group, participants will listen to a podcast concerning soft skills related to social attitudes."

issues.subcategory: unequal timing and engagement across conditions
issues.description: The Demonstration and motivation condition includes a DRM memory task, feedback, and a motivational podcast, whereas other conditions appear to involve only approximately seven-minute podcasts. This creates differences in retention interval, cognitive load, fatigue, attention, emotional arousal, and experimenter contact that can independently affect memory performance.
issues.quote: "The extended warning will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast" ... "The training will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast" ... "First, in order to demonstrate to participants that they are vulnerable to influence, a substantially shortened and simplified procedure based on the DRM paradigm will be used"

issues.description: The study does not specify checks that participants attended to, understood, believed, or were affected by the podcasts, warning, DRM demonstration, or motivational message. Without manipulation checks, null effects may reflect failed delivery and positive effects may be difficult to interpret mechanistically.
issues.quote: "Participants in the ‘Extended warning’ group will listen to the podcast" ... "those in in the ‘Education about memory’ group will listen to the podcast" ... "Participants in the DRM group will be given the DRM procedure with feedback"

issues.description: The theoretical account depends heavily on participants being aware of discrepancies between their own memory and the co-witness information, yet the study does not include a direct measure of discrepancy awareness or source monitoring at the item level. Therefore the main proposed mechanism cannot be tested.
issues.quote: "Thus, we expect that effectiveness of our methods will be higher among people aware of discrepancies between the original information and misinformation than among those unaware of such discrepancies."

issues.description: The manuscript claims normative influence is completely ruled out because the final test is individual. This is too strong: prior public agreement, commitment to a joint answer, anticipated evaluation, co-witness presence, and internalized social pressure can still influence later individual responses. Overstating this assumption narrows interpretation unjustifiably.
issues.quote: "we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect is completely ruled out in this study: participants work on their own and do not compare their answers with anybody, therefore there is no cost of disagreeing."

issues.description: The study plans to assess awareness of the real purpose after the final test, but at least one intervention explicitly explains the deception and source of discrepancies before the final test. Thus awareness is experimentally induced in some conditions and cannot be used as an unbiased exploratory predictor of performance.
issues.quote: "In addition, the podcast will explain why the deception was applied." ... "Next, the subjects will be requested to say what they think the real purpose of the study was. Their responses will be recorded for exploratory analysis of any relationship between hypothesis awareness and performance."

issues.description: The manuscript states that pairs or participants will be randomly assigned but does not describe the randomization method, allocation concealment, blocking, stratification, or whether assignment is by participant or dyad. This limits reproducibility and raises the possibility of imbalance across conditions.
issues.quote: "Pairs of participants will be randomly assigned to one of four groups"

issues.description: Memory conformity is affected by familiarity, trust, age, gender, dominance, and perceived credibility, but the study provides little control or measurement of dyad composition beyond broad age restrictions. Unequal distribution of these factors across conditions could confound intervention effects.
issues.quote: "The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old; they will be invited to participate via advertisements in the media and on the internet."

issues.description: Participants as young as 16 will be enrolled, but the manuscript does not mention parental consent, assent, ethics approval, or special protections for minors exposed to deception and potentially distressing information about wrongful convictions. This is an important ethical and reporting omission.
issues.quote: "The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old"

issues.description: The MORI manipulation and critical details depend on visual perception, including color discrimination, and interventions depend on hearing and language comprehension. The manuscript does not specify screening for color blindness, visual impairments, hearing impairments, Polish fluency, or prior familiarity with the materials.
issues.quote: "in the first version, Eric is trying on a black hat, whereas in the second version the hat is red" ... "participants will listen to a podcast"

issues.description: The MORI technique requires participants to see only their assigned version and not notice the dual projection. The manuscript instructs participants not to peek but does not specify objective checks, suspicion probes before intervention, exclusion criteria for noticing double images, or verification that the glasses worked for each participant.
issues.quote: "Please make sure you watch the movie through the glasses (no peeking over the top or around the side)"

issues.description: The only stated exclusion criterion is technical problems. The plan does not address participants who fail to follow instructions, notice the deception prematurely, communicate after the discussion, have sensory problems, provide unusable data, or do not complete tasks. This threatens data quality and reproducibility.
issues.quote: "We will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems during the experimental session."

issues.description: Technical problems are not operationally defined and no procedure is given for documenting them, deciding exclusions blind to condition/outcome, or replacing excluded participants. This creates post hoc flexibility.
issues.quote: "We will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems during the experimental session."

issues.description: If the final test is open-ended, scoring requires coding ambiguous, partial, synonymous, missing, and multiple answers. The manuscript does not specify coding rules, coder training, blinding to condition, or inter-rater reliability, all of which are necessary to avoid bias and ensure reproducibility.
issues.quote: "The test will contain 20 open-ended questions" ... "Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test"

issues.subcategory: collaborative test may introduce non-social misinformation
issues.description: During the collaborative recognition test, participants see five possible responses for each question. These alternatives may themselves introduce misinformation independent of the partner's statements, making it difficult to attribute later errors specifically to co-witness influence.
issues.quote: "Each question and its five possible responses will be displayed in a PowerPoint presentation for 60 seconds while participants discuss the answer."

issues.description: The discussion is audio recorded, but the analysis plan does not specify transcription, coding of who said what, confidence, dominance, order of mention, agreement, or actual exposure to misinformation. Without item-level coding, the study cannot distinguish conformity to partner-provided misinformation from guessing, mutual agreement, or absence of misinformation.
issues.quote: "If the participants are unable to reach an agreement, both responses will be documented. The discussion will be audio recorded."

issues.description: The manuscript does not clearly state whether participants are separated after collaborative recall or prevented from further communication while listening to interventions and before the individual test. Additional discussion could contaminate the individual memory test and reintroduce social influence.
issues.quote: "After that, the third phase will take place: it will consist in the procedures to reduce vulnerability to misinformation that were described above." ... "Immediately after the participants are done with the methods of reducing memory conformity (or the control condition), they will complete the individual memory test"

issues.subcategory: DRM manipulation may fail for some participants
issues.description: The Demonstration and motivation intervention depends on participants falsely recalling critical lures. The manuscript acknowledges only that most participants usually do so and gives no plan for participants who do not produce false memories. For those participants, the demonstration may fail or even increase confidence in their memory.
issues.quote: "The DRM procedure usually results in most of the participants falsely recalling at least a few of the critical lures." ... "If so, you were fooled."

issues.description: The podcasts and DRM materials are described only generally and are not reproduced in full. Without scripts, word lists, timing, delivery details, and validation/piloting information, the interventions are difficult to replicate and their equivalence cannot be evaluated.
issues.quote: "The extended warning will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast about the fallibility of human memory." ... "The training will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast discussing the mechanisms of memory" ... "Four lists will be chosen which on the basis of our previous research with this procedure, produce the strongest effect."

issues.description: The experimenter administers condition-specific procedures and the study uses open-ended responses, but there is no statement that experimenters or coders will be blinded to condition or hypotheses. Knowledge of condition could influence task delivery, participant interaction, or scoring.
issues.quote: "Participants in the DRM group will be given the DRM procedure with feedback" ... "the experimenter will give the following information to the participants"

issues.description: The plan says DRM results will be used as a predictor of MORI results, but the DRM task is administered only in the Demonstration and motivation condition. Any association is therefore condition-specific, potentially underpowered, and confounded with receiving that intervention.
issues.quote: "As an additional exploratory analysis, the results on the DRM procedure will be used as a possible predictor of the results on the MORI technique."

issues.description: The study uses a brief silent movie, a small number of object details, and a convenience sample aged 16–35 recruited through advertisements. These features limit generalization to real eyewitness contexts, older witnesses, children, high-stress events, and longer retention intervals, but the manuscript makes broad justice-system claims.
issues.quote: "the participants will watch a silent movie that lasts 6 minutes and 34 seconds" ... "The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old; they will be invited to participate via advertisements in the media and on the internet."

issues.description: The rationale states that the most effective approach is to prepare witnesses before misinformation reaches them, but the procedure places the interventions after collaborative recall. Therefore the study, as procedurally described, does not test the claimed real-world inoculation use case.
issues.quote: "we wanted to inoculate participants against the influence of misinformation before it could take effect. In reality, it is most effective to prepare a witness before possible misinformation reaches them."

issues.description: The study collects confidence ratings for every answer but does not specify confirmatory analyses involving confidence, calibration, or confidence-accuracy relationships. This is a missed opportunity and creates additional researcher degrees of freedom if confidence is later analyzed selectively.
issues.quote: "for each question, the participants will be asked to rate the subjective certainty of each answer on a scale from 0% (complete uncertainty, guessing) to 100% (absolute certainty)."

issues.description: The manuscript does not describe how missing responses, incomplete sessions, ambiguous answers, equipment failures, or participant withdrawal will be handled analytically. This omission affects reproducibility and may bias estimates if missingness differs by condition.
issues.quote: "Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test: the number of: (1) correct answers (consistent with the movie), (2) answers consistent with the misinformation, (3) other answers (consistent neither with the movie nor the misinformation), and (4) the overall number of answers."

issues.subcategory: intervention may alter response criterion rather than memory
issues.description: Warnings, education, and motivation may change willingness to answer, willingness to say 'don't know,' or reliance on guessing rather than memory accuracy. Although the manuscript counts the overall number of answers, it does not specify analyses that distinguish memory accuracy from response criterion shifts.
issues.quote: "Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test: the number of: (1) correct answers (consistent with the movie), (2) answers consistent with the misinformation, (3) other answers (consistent neither with the movie nor the misinformation), and (4) the overall number of answers."
